body: From the taper-tantrum low (Sensex ~18,000, Aug-Sept 2013) the market re-rated on expectations of a decisive BJP win: Nifty crossed 7,000 around exit polls (May 2014) and the Sensex touched 25,000 intraday on results day, 16 May 2014; the Sensex then peaked near ~30,000 intraday in March 2015 (levels from memory). Calendar 2014 returns (from memory, unverified): Sensex ~+30%, BSE Midcap ~+55%, BSE Smallcap ~+69% - small caps led strongly. Leaders: PSU banks, capital goods, infra, cyclicals, mid/small caps that had been most beaten down; laggards: defensives (FMCG, pharma) on a relative basis. Valuation: Sensex P/E re-rated from ~15-16x to ~19-20x as earnings stayed flat - the move was hope. What followed: earnings disappointed for years (FY15-FY20 Nifty EPS growth was weak), the RBI's 2015 asset-quality review exposed PSU bank NPAs, and the Sensex fell ~25% to ~22,500 by Feb 2016. Signal visible at the time: the rally was P/E-driven with no earnings upgrades, and PSU banks rallied while stressed loans rose. Lesson: political change can trigger a sharp rerating from depressed valuations - the best returns came from buying the despair of 2013, not the euphoria of 2014-15; ratings without earnings fade.
title: 2014 Modi election rally (Sept 2013 - Mar 2015)
